look_here_first: Examine stem and node hairs with magnification: O. stricta often shows spreading hairs, including SEPTATE hairs at nodes, rather than the densely straight, forward-appressed NONSEPTATE hairs of O. dillenii. Check flower-cluster size and mature capsules only as supporting traits.

project_inclusion.range_basis: FNA and POWO do not list Texas as native for this accepted concept, whereas the project Hays source pool includes it. Texas native status and source ID remain a voucher-level conflict; no target-zone PASS.

morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous woodsorrel with upright to spreading leafy stems; habit overlaps O. dillenii and can be altered by mowing.
morphology_keys.leaves: Trifoliolate with notched, heartlike leaflets; leaf outline alone does not distinguish similar yellow Oxalis.
morphology_keys.stems: Hairs often spreading, with a mix of septate and nonseptate hairs; septate hairs particularly informative at stem nodes.
morphology_keys.flowers: Yellow five-petaled flowers, often several per inflorescence (frequently 5–7); petals typically 8–11 mm but variable.
morphology_keys.fruit: Slender capsule commonly 8–15 mm; fruit length alone is not decisive.

comparisons.key_distinctions: O. dillenii usually has straight forward-appressed nonseptate hairs, fewer flowers (often 1–3), and longer 12–20 mm capsules. O. albicans has short curved/crisped nonseptate hairs; O. corniculata may root at prostrate nodes and has conspicuous broad free stipules.
comparisons.cautions: Texas source-pool record is not verified as this taxon; do not count as Texas/target-zone native or infer invasive status. Photos may be identified under broad O. stricta concepts. Recheck hairs with a microscope and preserve uncertainty.

diagnostic_image_needs: Macro of spreading SEPTATE stem hairs, especially at nodes

Mature capsules with length and seed close-up
